name: org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin
description: GW Maven Plugin is the primary Maven adapter for the Machai Ghostwriter application. It integrates Ghostwriter guided file processing into Apache Maven so Java teams can run AI-assisted documentation maintenance, prompt-driven actions, source and site file updates, embedded @guidance processing, and cleanup tasks from normal Maven build workflows. The plugin provides goals for execution-root orchestration and per-module reactor execution, understands Maven project metadata, module ordering, source roots, compiled output directories, dependency classpaths, Maven settings credentials, and optional GenAI provider configuration. It is useful for maintaining project documentation, site content, source-adjacent guidance files, and other project files in Java and Maven projects. It includes Maven goals gw:gw, gw:gw-per-module, gw:act, gw:act-per-module, and gw:clean, plus function tools for discovering Java classes and reading reflective class metadata from project and dependency classpaths.

usageContext: AI-assisted file processing using embedded guidance tags
Interactive and predefined prompt actions over project files
Class discovery and reflective metadata lookup for AI workflows

constructors.description: Creates a function-tool provider backed by the supplied Maven project. The instance scans and caches class metadata for the project base directory so AI workflows can find classes and inspect reflective metadata using the current Maven project classpath, output directories, and dependency artifacts.

examples.description: Creates project-aware class function tools inside Maven plugin code. The project value is supplied by Maven runtime components, then the tools can be registered with the Ghostwriter processor for class lookup and metadata inspection.

constructors.description: Creates an empty class function-tool provider. Projects must be registered later with scanProjectClasses before findClass or getClassInfo can resolve metadata for a project context.

examples.description: Creates the tools first and registers a Maven project later. This pattern is useful when a processor is initialized before the current MavenProject is available.

constructors.description: Creates a holder for class discovery and lookup data for one Maven project. It builds a dedicated java.net.URLClassLoader from the compile classpath and main and test output directories, scans visible classes, records source paths, and maps dependency classes to Maven artifact coordinates where possible.

examples.description: Creates a direct class metadata holder and searches for Maven Mojo classes by simple class-name regular expression.

features.name: gw:gw
features.description: Runs Ghostwriter guided file processing as an aggregator Maven goal. It can run without a pom.xml in the current directory, scans selected files for embedded guidance instructions, processes modules in reverse order so submodules can be handled before parent modules, and forwards model, path, instructions, excludes, server credentials, input logging, and threading configuration to the workflow.

examples.description: Runs guided processing for files under src/site using the selected GenAI model. Use this when documentation or site files contain embedded @guidance blocks that should be updated by Ghostwriter.

features.name: gw:gw-per-module
features.description: Runs guided document processing once per Maven module in the active reactor. Maven determines module execution order using the standard reactor dependency graph. The goal reuses shared scanning and GenAI configuration from AbstractGWMojo and binds Maven-specific layout metadata for each processed module.

examples.description: Processes each reactor module, limits scanning to each module site directory, applies additional instructions, and skips generated or external directories.

features.name: gw:act
features.description: Runs an interactive or predefined action prompt over a documentation tree. If gw.act is not provided, the goal prompts the user through Maven's Plexus Prompter. It supports custom act definitions via gw.acts and inherits common model, path, excludes, instructions, credentials, and logging configuration.

examples.description: Runs a practical prompt-driven action against Markdown site files. The command is useful for one-off documentation refactoring tasks that do not require embedded guidance blocks.

features.name: gw:act-per-module
features.description: Runs an action prompt in a reactor-friendly per-module context. It is intended for standard Maven reactor builds, requires a Maven project, delegates scanning to ActProcessor, and supports the same act and shared configuration parameters as ActMojo and AbstractGWMojo.

examples.description: Invokes the same documentation summarization action for each module in the reactor while respecting Maven module execution behavior.

features.name: gw:clean
features.description: Deletes temporary artifacts created by Machai Ghostwriter document processing. This goal is normally associated with cleanup workflows and may be bound to Maven's clean lifecycle.

examples.description: Removes temporary workflow artifacts for the current Maven module or project after guided processing runs.

features.name: findClass
features.description: Finds fully qualified class names whose simple class names match a supplied regular expression. The search is resolved against a registered Maven project base directory and uses class metadata scanned from project outputs and compile classpath dependencies.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools(currentMavenProject);
java.lang.String matches = tools.findClass(".*Mojo", currentMavenProject.getBasedir());
examples.description: Searches the current Maven project for classes whose simple names end in Mojo, returning fully qualified class names that can be inspected with getClassInfo.

features.name: getClassInfo
features.description: Returns reflective metadata for a fully qualified Java class. The result may include modifiers, superclass, interfaces, non-private fields, constructors, non-private methods, annotations, class path, dependency artifact coordinates, source path, or an error message when resolution fails.

examples.description: Inspects the GWMojo class and returns structured metadata for AI-assisted reasoning about available methods, inheritance, annotations, and source location.

customizations.name: gw.model
customizations.description: Configuration property that selects the provider and model identifier forwarded to Ghostwriter processing, for example CodeMie:gpt-5.5-2026-04-24 or another provider-specific model id.

examples.description: Runs the guided processing goal with an explicit GenAI model selection.

customizations.name: gw.path
customizations.description: Configuration property that selects the scan root for files to process. If omitted, defaults depend on the selected goal and Maven execution context.

examples.description: Processes only Markdown files and related content under the selected documentation directory.

customizations.name: genai.serverId
customizations.description: Configuration property that identifies a Maven settings.xml server entry. The plugin reads matching credentials and custom XML configuration values and forwards them to the processing pipeline.

examples.description: Configures Maven credentials once in settings.xml and references them by server id when invoking the plugin.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.AbstractGWMojo
studs.description: Base class for GW Maven plugin goals. It centralizes shared configuration and the common scan and execute flow, resolves optional GenAI credentials from Maven settings.xml, registers class-related helper tools when a Maven project is present, and delegates document scanning to Ghostwriter processors.

examples.description: Shows how a custom Maven goal could extend the shared base class and reuse common Ghostwriter configuration and scanning behavior.

examples.title: Install and configure the Maven plugin in a project POM
steps: Add org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.2.2 to the build plugins section of pom.xml.
Set model, serverId, path, instructions, excludes, logInputs, or threads as needed.
Place embedded @guidance blocks in source, site, documentation, or other project files that should be maintained by Ghostwriter.
Run a plugin goal such as gw:gw or gw:act from the project root.
examples.description: This scenario installs the ready-to-use Maven plugin and configures it for documentation processing under src/site.

examples.title: Configure provider credentials in Maven settings.xml
steps: Open the user or CI Maven settings.xml file.
Add a server entry whose id matches the genai.serverId or serverId value used by the plugin.
Store provider username, password, and optional custom configuration values in that server entry.
Run the plugin with -Dgenai.serverId=CodeMie or configure serverId in pom.xml.
examples.description: This scenario keeps provider credentials out of the project POM and lets the plugin resolve them through Maven settings integration.

examples.title: Run guided processing for site documentation
steps: Ensure Markdown or other project files contain @guidance instructions.
Choose the scan directory with gw.path.
Provide the GenAI model and optional server id.
Run the gw goal and review the resulting file changes.
examples.description: This practical command updates site Markdown using embedded guidance tags and logs the input file list for traceability.

examples.title: Run a one-off action over project documentation
steps: Decide on the prompt action to apply.
Choose a scan path that limits the action to the intended files.
Invoke gw:act with the prompt in gw.act.
Review the produced modifications before committing them.
examples.snippet: mvn org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.2.2:act -Dgw.act="Rewrite headings for clarity and consistency" -Dgw.path=src/site/markdown
examples.description: This scenario demonstrates prompt-driven maintenance without adding embedded guidance blocks to every file.

examples.title: Process each module in a Maven reactor
steps: Use a multi-module Maven project with modules declared in the parent POM.
Select the per-module goal for normal reactor execution semantics.
Provide path, instructions, excludes, and model configuration as needed.
Run the command from the reactor root.
examples.description: This scenario applies guided processing module by module, matching Maven reactor behavior for larger Java projects.
